marketAlerts.change: DOJ moves to seize $1.2B stolen in the Binance hack as Binance says it has fully covered user losses
marketAlerts.summary: The US Justice Department said on Nov 12 it has court authorization to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion of the crypto stolen from Binance on or about Oct 29 by North Korean military hackers the FBI calls TraderTraitor. That sits inside more than $2.7 billion frozen so far by US authorities and private firms, which Bloomberg Law reports was largely frozen by Tether and Circle, and tracing continues as the hackers launder through bridges, mixers and exchanges. The same release said the FBI seized cloud infrastructure behind FaceStealer, a deepfake video-call scheme that has stolen more than $400 million from crypto and Web3 users over 18 months. Earlier that day Binance said it had completed coverage of the roughly $6.3 billion of affected assets and published a new proof-of-reserves snapshot.
marketAlerts.why: Freezing almost half of the largest crypto theft on record limits how much North Korea can cash out and shows stablecoin issuers and exchanges acting quickly with law enforcement. The FaceStealer warning is directly relevant to anyone in crypto who takes unexpected video calls.

marketAlerts.change: Trezor confirms hidden seed-stealing implants in Safe 5 wallets sold by a reseller and cuts its reseller network by 80%
marketAlerts.summary: Trezor published the results of its CryptoBilis investigation: Safe 5 devices bought from that Southeast Asian reseller between Aug 20 and Sep 23, 2026 may contain an added circuit board that captures recovery words and passphrases shown on screen and sends them over a mobile network. Trezor confirmed the implant in three devices, released firmware 2.13.1 on Nov 11 to stop the identified implants capturing new data, and said it has cut its reseller network by about 80%. It tells affected buyers to update and move funds to a new wallet with a new seed phrase, because anything already captured stays compromised. No losses tied to these devices were reported in the coverage reviewed.
marketAlerts.why: It is a hardware supply-chain attack on self-custody, the second such reseller case reported for a major wallet maker this month, and it affects users on every chain. Buying wallets only from the manufacturer or authorized sellers is the practical defense.

news.title: DFINITY launches Cloud Engines, private Internet Computer subnets pitched as a sovereign cloud for AI, with 20% of revenue set to buy and burn ICP
news.body: DFINITY introduced Cloud Engines on Nov 13, calling it a sovereign cloud built to keep running through cyberattacks and data-center outages and to host AI agents and apps. Organizations assemble their own private Internet Computer subnet, from a minimum of four nodes, by choosing node providers, locations and hardware through opencloud.org; apps run as canisters and can use HTTPS outcalls and verifiable randomness. Early access is open with developer coupons issued from the week of Nov 10, and Crypto Briefing reports commercial release is set for mid-November. Under DFINITY's Mission 70 token plan, 20% of Cloud Engines revenue goes to buying and burning ICP and 80% to node providers. No customers, pricing or usage figures were published.
news.why: This is the product DFINITY has been building toward since Internet Computer 2.0, and it is the first direct link between paid enterprise cloud usage and ICP supply. Whether it matters depends entirely on paying customers; with no adoption data yet, the burn is a mechanism, not a measured effect.
news.tagReason: A long-promised commercial product ships with a revenue-to-burn link for ICP.
news.summary: DFINITY introduced Cloud Engines on Nov 13, calling it a sovereign cloud built to keep running through cyberattacks and data-center outages and to host AI agents and apps.

news.title: Polkadot adopts a user-first strategy with dotUSD at its core, and a second validator cut to 400 is set for Nov 18 if it passes
news.body: Polkadot said on Nov 13 that a new strategy proposed by the Polkadot Community Foundation was approved on Nov 11 with about 97% of votes (Referendum 1954). It focuses resources on direct user acquisition for an upcoming mobile-first product platform, starting with the Polkadot App's private messaging and digital-cash payments, and shifts shared funds from general marketing to incentives tied to measurable user activity. It also makes dotUSD and other DOT-backed stable assets, overseen by the Technical Fellowship, the main way to create demand for DOT. Separately, Referendum 1969, submitted Nov 11 and still in voting with near-unanimous support so far, would cut the active validator set from 500 to 400 around midday CET on Nov 18; CryptoTicker notes the 400th-place validator already carries about 1.68 million DOT of backing.
news.why: It is the clearest statement yet of how Polkadot intends to turn usage into DOT demand, moving away from a parachain-first story toward consumer apps and stablecoins. The validator cut, if enacted, lowers security costs but concentrates stake, and nominators backing lower-ranked validators may need to re-nominate before Nov 18.
news.tagReason: A strong governance mandate, but the product and dotUSD demand are still to be proven.
news.summary: Polkadot said on Nov 13 that a new strategy proposed by the Polkadot Community Foundation was approved on Nov 11 with about 97% of votes (Referendum 1954).

news.title: Hyperliquid's Q3: record $16.8B open interest passes Bybit, Kraken and OKX, with $191M revenue
news.body: A Hyperliquid Research Collective report covered by The Block on Nov 13 says Hyperliquid ended Q3 with a record $16.8 billion in open interest, up nearly 80% from the end of June, enough to pass Bybit, Kraken and OKX. Its share of open interest across Hyperliquid and eight major exchanges rose to 11.7% from 9.6%, native perpetuals volume climbed from $109.5 billion in July to more than $188 billion in September, and quarterly revenue rose 22% to $191 million as daily traders hit a record. Stock-linked perpetuals on HIP-3 markets grew 161%, overtaking commodities. The report also notes trading firms such as Wintermute paying for early looks at incoming orders, which has raised fairness questions.
news.why: It is evidence that Hyperliquid's growth is broad and fee-producing, not just token incentives, and that it now competes directly with top centralized derivatives venues. The figures come from a community research group, not audited filings, and the priority-data auctions are a market-structure concern to watch.
news.tagReason: Record open interest and revenue show real trading demand on the network.
news.summary: A Hyperliquid Research Collective report covered by The Block on Nov 13 says Hyperliquid ended Q3 with a record $16.8 billion in open interest, up nearly 80% from the end of June, enough to pass Bybit, Kraken and OKX.

news.title: Solana Confidential Compute enters devnet beta, verifying private-AI hardware onchain
news.body: The Solana Foundation and Nito released Solana Confidential Compute on Nov 13, an open-source SDK and onchain program that checks hardware attestations from trusted execution environments and publishes a public record on Solana. That lets apps, agents and users confirm that private data was processed inside genuine confidential-computing hardware running the expected software. Coverage says it supports Intel TDX and AMD SEV-SNP today, with NVIDIA GPU attestation still in development. It is a beta on devnet only; mainnet is promised after a security audit, and Nito is the first platform building on it.
news.why: Private AI is becoming a contested category (NEAR, Sui and others are pitching the same thing), and onchain attestations give Solana a verifiable answer. It is unaudited devnet code, so this is developer tooling, not production usage.
news.tagReason: New open-source infrastructure extends Solana into verifiable private AI.
news.summary: The Solana Foundation and Nito released Solana Confidential Compute on Nov 13, an open-source SDK and onchain program that checks hardware attestations from trusted execution environments and publishes a public record on Solana.

news.title: Glamsterdam stays on hold: Ethereum developers wait for audits on gas repricing before setting a new testnet date
news.body: Ethereum's next upgrade, Glamsterdam, still has no Hoodi testnet or mainnet date after its Oct 26 Hoodi activation was postponed. The pause traces to EIP-8037 and EIP-8038, which change how gas is charged for state, after ChainSecurity found deployed contracts relying on assumptions those changes would break; by Nov 9 the Ethereum Foundation had four community reports of contracts that could be affected, still under review. ChainSecurity and Dedaub audit reports were due Nov 13 (not yet posted at midday Central, per stakefish), findings go to the Nov 16 testing call, and the Nov 19 All Core Devs call will discuss next steps, including possible spec revisions. Work on the following upgrade, Hegotá, continues in parallel.
news.why: Gas repricing is central to Glamsterdam's scaling goals, so any revision changes what the upgrade delivers and when. Next week's two calls are the decision points; stakers and node operators have nothing to do yet.
news.tagReason: A cautious delay to protect deployed contracts, not a failure.
news.summary: Ethereum's next upgrade, Glamsterdam, still has no Hoodi testnet or mainnet date after its Oct 26 Hoodi activation was postponed.

news.title: XRPL Lending Protocol reaches 22 of 35 validator votes, still short of activation
news.body: Support for native lending on the XRP Ledger reached 22 of 35 validators on Nov 13, according to ICOBench's tracking of the amendment vote. The upgrade pairs Single Asset Vaults (XLS-65), pooled deposits of XRP or stablecoins such as RLUSD, with the Lending Protocol (XLS-66), which issues fixed-term loans from those vaults while brokers handle credit checks off-ledger. Amendments need 80% validator support held for two weeks before they switch on, so the count is still several votes short. ICOBench's pace estimate puts activation around January 2027, which is a projection, not a schedule.
news.why: Native credit is the main missing piece of Ripple's institutional DeFi pitch for XRPL, and it would give RLUSD and XRP a lending use on the ledger itself. Until it clears the threshold it is a pending vote, and the vote count should be checked against an XRPL amendment explorer.
news.tagReason: Progress toward a key feature, but activation is not yet assured.

news.title: Tesla invites select customers to buy the Cybercab for personal use at $29,990 plus a $299 monthly autonomy subscription
news.body: Tesla said on Nov 13 it is inviting select customers to buy the two-seat Cybercab for personal use, priced at $29,990 with a required $299-a-month Autonomy Subscription, Reuters reports. Elon Musk said it would be offered nationwide as regulatory approvals arrive and that the monthly fee is too high and should match Full Self-Driving pricing of about $115. Tesla's AI head said the Cybercab will run unsupervised in the same areas as its robotaxi service, which operates in Austin, Dallas, Houston and Miami.
news.why: It is Tesla's first step toward selling a car with no manual controls to consumers, making autonomy a subscription business. Uptake depends on regulatory approval outside current robotaxi areas.
news.tagReason: A new autonomy product reaches consumers.

news.title: Google adds Gemini 4 Hydrogen and a multi-model Orchestrator to its Antigravity coding environment
news.body: Google introduced Gemini 4 Hydrogen on Nov 13, a lighter, lower-cost execution model, and added Orchestrator to Antigravity, its AI development environment. Orchestrator hands planning to a model such as Gemini 4 Carbon or Argon and execution (editing files, writing code, running builds and tests) to Hydrogen within one session, which Google says cuts token use. It follows Gemini 4 Carbon's broad release on Nov 10.
news.why: Cheaper execution models aimed at coding agents compete directly for the fastest-growing source of paid AI usage. Savings claims are Google's own.
news.tagReason: New lower-cost model and coding tooling.

news.title: Meta tests 'Takes', a points-based prediction-market app, with employees
news.body: Meta has begun internal testing of a prediction-market app called Takes in which users wager 'cred' points rather than money, The Wall Street Journal reported on Nov 13, as covered by The Block. The project was first reported in June under the name Arena. Meta declined to comment or give a timetable, and the report does not say whether real-money contracts remain possible.
news.why: Prediction markets are one of crypto's biggest consumer categories, so a Meta entry, even points-only, could bring the format to billions of users. It is an unconfirmed internal test, with real-money platforms tied up in state lawsuits.
news.tagReason: An internal test reported by WSJ; not announced by Meta.

news.body: Mercury Research's Q3 2026 data, reported Nov 13, show AMD's desktop CPU share falling about 5.1 points to 29.9%, with Intel at about 70.1%. Coverage attributes the shift to Intel moving capacity from weaker laptop demand into desktops and AMD prioritizing higher-margin data-center and AI products. AMD's server CPU share rose to 35.5%.
news.why: It is a rare client-market gain for Intel, while AMD's mix shift toward servers matches where AI spending is. Quarterly share swings can reverse.

news.body: Two days moved tokenized stocks from crypto-native wrappers toward core market plumbing. On Nov 11 xStocks put 200+ 1:1-backed UK and EU equities onchain with Solana and Ethereum among its launch chains (not available in the US or to UK investors). The backdrop is the NYSE's choice, announced just before this window, of an Avalanche-based chain. None of the US-regulated pieces trades yet.
news.why: Solana is now the common thread across DTCC, xStocks and Ondo integrations, which strengthens its claim as the main venue for tokenized securities, while Ethereum keeps parallel access. Timelines run into 2027 and depend on approvals, so this is structural positioning rather than current volume.

news.title: Apex Group, which services $3.5 trillion in assets, joins the Hedera Council
news.body: Hedera announced on Nov 11 that Apex Group, a fund administrator and financial-services provider servicing more than $3.5 trillion in assets, has joined the Hedera Council, the body that governs the network. Council members vote on software upgrades, network pricing and treasury decisions, sign governance transactions and run a mainnet node; membership is a governance role and does not entitle members to treasury HBAR. Apex says it will explore Hedera for its tokenization work, including asset-lifecycle management, compliance and settlement, and its digital-assets head stressed the ERC-3643 compliant-token standard. Apex already owns a majority of Tokeny, which integrated with Hedera in April 2025. The announcement describes exploration, not a committed product or volume on Hedera.
news.why: A large regulated fund administrator taking a governance seat strengthens Hedera's institutional tokenization pitch and adds an operator with real asset-servicing scale. The value to the network depends on whether Apex actually issues or services funds on Hedera, which has not been announced yet.
news.tagReason: A major fund administrator joins Hedera's governing council and plans tokenization work on the network.

news.title: Flare goes from emergency fork to outward expansion in three days
news.body: Flare spotted an exploit attempt against upstream Avalanche-based node code and fast-tracked go-flare v1.15.1 on Nov 10; the mainnet fork activated cleanly at 8:00 AM CST on Nov 11, and Flare says user funds and keys were never affected. Firelight published its cover limits the same day (up to 5.7% of TVL on Lido's EarnETH vault and 8% on EarnUSD). On Nov 12 Flare announced its LayerZero verifier service for cross-chain tokens, due in early December, and an order book for XRP yield on Spectra. The dashboard's Flare value-locked alert (now −19.1% over 7 days) has no verified cause. On Nov 13 Flare published a developer walkthrough of how issuers add its DVN to an OFT setup.
news.why: A clean response to a security scare followed by an external product launch is a constructive sequence for the network beneath FXRP and Firelight. A post-mortem on the exploit attempt and a recovery in value locked are still outstanding.
news.tagReason: Security risk resolved and a new product announced, while value locked keeps falling.

news.title: Allium report puts Stellar at $4.1B of tokenized real-world assets and a 91% rise in stablecoin supply
news.body: The Stellar Development Foundation published a report by data firm Allium on Nov 11 on institutional finance on Stellar. It says tokenized real-world assets on Stellar reached $4.12 billion, up about 6.1 times over the 12 months to September 2026, with Stellar's share of tokenized assets rising from 4.9% to 12.7%; Stellar's account says the figure is now above $5 billion. The report puts Stellar stablecoin supply up 91% to $546 million over the period, against roughly flat industry growth, and stablecoin transfer volume up 127%, plus $319 million of non-US debt issued. It includes case studies on MoneyGram, Spiko, FTDA_US and others. The figures cover the period to September and come from a report promoted by Stellar itself. On Nov 12 Stellar also cited Token Terminal data ranking it the No. 2 chain for tokenized funds, with 6.7 times growth in a year.
news.why: It is a data-backed case that Stellar's payments-and-tokenization focus is turning into real assets on the ledger, which matters more than conference announcements. Most of the RWA total sits with a small number of large issuers, so concentration is the caveat.
news.tagReason: Independent data shows strong year-over-year growth in Stellar RWAs and stablecoins.
news.summary: The Stellar Development Foundation published a report by data firm Allium on Nov 11 on institutional finance on Stellar.

news.title: Bankr opens index-token creation to everyone on Base and Robinhood Chain
news.body: Bankr said on Nov 11 that index tokens are now open to all users. Anyone can create an ERC-20 index holding 2 to 20 tokens or tokenized stocks with custom weights on Base or Robinhood Chain, starting with a $100 first buy, and set a trading fee between 0.25% and 1%; creators can also launch a coin paired with the index. Bankr's docs say the creator's initial tokens are locked for 24 hours and publish a developer guide for creating and rebalancing indexes programmatically or from an agent. On Nov 13 Bankr said it has powered more than $5 billion of trading volume on Base and $20 million-plus of creator fees, and previewed a Token SDK; 17 teams are building for the Base Stocks Maxxing program through Dec 5.

news.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO; CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO
news.body: Nvidia said on Nov 12 that its board accepted Jensen Huang's resignation as president, CEO and director on Nov 11, effective immediately, according to its 8-K filing. CFO Colette Kress becomes interim CEO while keeping the CFO role, and longtime director Harvey C. Jones becomes the board's first chair; the board will consider internal and external candidates for a permanent CEO. AP and TechCrunch report the resignation followed revelations of an affair that raised national-security concerns, which the board had been investigating since Nov 8. Nvidia says operations, customer commitments and the product roadmap continue without interruption, and Q3 fiscal 2027 results remain scheduled for Nov 17.
news.why: Losing the founder-CEO who led Nvidia for 33 years is the biggest leadership change in the AI-chip industry, and it lands days before a closely watched earnings report. Execution risk now centers on succession and on how the national-security questions are resolved.
news.tagReason: An abrupt founder-CEO exit under national-security scrutiny.
news.summary: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO; CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO and Harvey Jones becomes board chair.

news.title: Google brings the Gemini app and Gemini Live to Apple CarPlay worldwide
news.body: Google said on Nov 11 that the Gemini app is rolling out globally on Apple CarPlay to all Gemini users on iOS in every supported Gemini Live language, following earlier launches on Android Auto and cars with Google built-in. Drivers can hold hands-free conversations to check calendars, summarize Gmail threads, get a daily brief or rehearse presentations, and the chats sync back to the iPhone app. Some personalization features, including Daily Brief, are not available to users under 18, in the European Economic Area or in Nigeria.
news.why: Getting Gemini onto Apple's in-car platform puts Google's assistant in front of iPhone users in a daily, high-frequency setting where Apple controls the screen. It is a distribution win for Gemini usage rather than a direct revenue line.
news.tagReason: Gemini gains a global distribution channel on Apple's in-car platform.
news.summary: Google rolled out the Gemini app and Gemini Live on Apple CarPlay globally on Nov 11.

weeklyRecap.title: Week in context · Nov 4–10, 2026
weeklyRecap.body:
The week's main theme was distribution moving into regulated and mainstream channels. Solana gained Formation's SEC-exemption notice for a tokenized-securities venue, a Schwab Crypto listing, a native privacy layer from Helius and one-tap trading from X cashtags; NEAR Intents went live in Talos's institutional system; HYPE gained won markets on Upbit and Bithumb plus the Elysium L2; and Ondo brought Fidelity's FCAT into every tokenized-stock bridge transfer. Bittensor's Gamma Tokens went live as a protocol payment rail, though first-day use was tiny.

Governance moved from votes to execution. Polkadot enacted Referendum 1966's 500-validator target on Nov 10, while Acala and Karura proposed shutting down in February 2027. Render's RNP-024 closed with only yes votes shown but no official announcement, and the XRPL Foundation's quantum-safe account design remains a draft with a 2027 study.

Security is the cross-watchlist caution. Flare forced an emergency hard fork after an exploit attempt, NEAR AI contained a cloud intrusion, and Elliptic traced Binance-hack laundering through NEAR memecoins. Market-wide incidents at Keplr/Web3Auth, LNbits, Ankr, Arcus, Initia and Across were each below the High threshold. Nothing in this recap is a price forecast or financial advice.

stocks.name: Tesla, Inc.
stocks.overview: Tesla builds electric vehicles and energy-storage systems and is investing heavily in self-driving (FSD, Robotaxi and the Cybercab), Optimus robots and its own AI compute. In Q3 2026 revenue was $28.05 billion, roughly flat year over year, with 486,532 deliveries (down about 2%) and net income attributable to common stockholders of $787 million ($0.22 per diluted share), down from $1.37 billion a year earlier; energy revenue fell 16% while services and other rose 33%. Recent moves include Cybercab service starting in Austin in September, a new €100 million Berlin engineering center that opened Nov 4 with about 250 staff, and an official Argentina launch set for Nov 20. Shareholders meet on Dec 3, and Tesla and SpaceX have discussed a possible combination, though no terms have been announced and any deal would need shareholder approval. The main near-term risk is political: after Democrats won Congress and Texas, Tesla and SpaceX shares fell about 11% and 9% on Nov 5, as investors priced in possible congressional probes and tighter rules on AI data centers.

stocks.name: Meta Platforms, Inc.
stocks.overview: Meta runs Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger, earns almost all of its revenue from advertising, and is spending heavily to build its Muse AI assistant and 'personal superintelligence'. Q3 2026 revenue rose 26% to $64.60 billion and diluted EPS was $3.83, or $7.40 excluding a $9.89 billion charge from its settlement with state attorneys general over teen mental health. Capital expenditures were $34.91 billion in the quarter and free cash flow was negative $2.12 billion. Meta expects 2026 capex of $135–145 billion and Q4 revenue of $73–76 billion. To fund the AI build-out it sold $15 billion of US-dollar bonds on Nov 3 and its first euro bonds (€9 billion) on Nov 4, and it has announced a non-voting Class C share class effective Jan 19, 2027. It launched Muse 'spaces' on Nov 6. The main risks are funding and returns on AI spending: S&P moved Meta's outlook to negative, and more youth-related trials are scheduled.
stocks.researchSummary: Meta's ad business is growing fast, but AI infrastructure spending has pushed free cash flow negative, so it is now raising large amounts of debt and planning equity. Product momentum in Muse continues, while litigation and data-center permitting after the midterms are the main watch items.
stocks.cryptoLink: Since April 2026, Meta has paid select creators in Colombia and the Philippines in Circle's USDC on Solana or Polygon via Stripe. It is not issuing its own stablecoin.

flags.text: Q3 included a $9.89 billion charge from a settlement with 52 state attorneys general of up to about $18.59 billion, and Meta says more youth-related trials are scheduled in the U.S. in the coming months.

Meta's capex of $135–145 billion turned Q3 free cash flow negative, S&P revised its outlook to AA- negative, and Meta's president said after the midterms that building data centers is 'going to be harder'.
Advertising was $63.06 billion of $64.60 billion in Q3 revenue. The new Class C structure is designed to keep Mark Zuckerberg in control, under a Founder Alignment Agreement.

stocks.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
stocks.overview: Alphabet owns Google Search, YouTube, Android, Google Cloud and the Gemini AI models, and sells its TPU AI chips through Google Cloud. Q3 2026 revenue rose 25% to $127.6 billion, Google Cloud revenue more than doubled (+103%) to $30.7 billion with $11.1 billion of operating income, and EPS was $2.12; the Gemini app has reached one billion users. This week Google announced a $15 billion data-center investment in Malaysia for 2027–2028 (Nov 4) and a $17 billion first data center in Laramie County, Wyoming (Nov 5), powered partly by a 702 MW Bloom fuel-cell system with carbon capture. Alphabet pays a $0.22 quarterly dividend on Dec 14 to holders of record on Dec 7. The main risk is legal: appeals are pending in both U.S. antitrust cases (search and ad tech), and a court refused to pause related private ad-tech suits.
stocks.researchSummary: Google Cloud is now Alphabet's fastest-growing engine, driven by AI infrastructure and TPU demand, and Google is committing tens of billions more to data centers even as U.S. local opposition grows. Antitrust remedies remain the key overhang.
stocks.cryptoLink: Google Cloud offers Universal Ledger, a managed, permissioned distributed ledger for tokenizing commercial bank money and securities and for wholesale payments.

stocks.name: NVIDIA Corporation
stocks.overview: Nvidia designs the GPUs, CPUs, networking and software that run most AI training and inference. On Nov 12 it announced that Jensen Huang had resigned as president, CEO and director, effective Nov 11; CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO while remaining CFO, Harvey C. Jones became the board's first chair, and the board is searching internal and external candidates. In Q2 fiscal 2027 (to July 26, 2026) revenue rose 106% to $96.2 billion with data center revenue of $89.0 billion, and Nvidia guided Q3 revenue to $108.0 billion ±2%, assuming no data-center compute revenue from China. Vera Rubin is in full production at major clouds, and Q3 FY27 results are still scheduled for Nov 17. The main risks are leadership succession, the national-security questions around Huang's departure, and export-policy scrutiny of China chip sales.
stocks.researchSummary: The business delivered another record quarter, but the abrupt exit of its founder-CEO makes the Nov 17 report and any succession news the key checkpoints. Nvidia says the roadmap and customer commitments are unchanged.

flags.text: Jensen Huang resigned as CEO and director effective Nov 11 after reports of an affair that raised national-security concerns; CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO and the board is searching for a permanent successor.

Semafor reports that Democrats taking over regulatory committees, along with Republicans pushing stronger export controls, point to closer scrutiny of Nvidia's China chip sales, possibly through the lame-duck defense bill and Senate Banking under Sen. Warren.

Board-led independent investigation announced Nov 8 after reports Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort; scope and timing not published.

stocks.name: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.
stocks.overview: AMD makes EPYC server CPUs, Instinct AI GPUs, Ryzen PC chips and embedded and gaming silicon. Q3 2026 revenue was a record $13.4 billion (+45%), data center revenue nearly doubled (+97%) to $8.5 billion on the MI450 launch and EPYC demand, and diluted EPS was $1.46 GAAP and $2.09 non-GAAP. Gaming revenue fell 40% to $773 million. AMD guided Q4 revenue to about $17 billion ±3% as it scales Helios rack systems and 'Venice' CPUs, and it filed its 10-Q on Nov 4. It is scheduled to present at the UBS conference on Dec 1 and Barclays on Dec 9. The main risk is AI-spending sentiment and supply: AMD shares fell double digits on Nov 5 in the post-midterm chip selloff, and the memory shortage is raising component costs.
stocks.researchSummary: AMD's latest quarter was its strongest on record and it is now mainly a data-center company, with guidance for faster growth in Q4. The stock's sharp drop on Nov 5 reflected sector-wide fears about the AI build-out rather than company-specific news.

stocks.name: Intel Corporation
stocks.overview: Intel designs and manufactures PC and server CPUs and is building a contract foundry business (Intel 14A). Q3 2026 revenue rose 21% to $16.5 billion, Data Center and AI revenue rose 78% to $7.3 billion (its strongest growth in 15 years) and Intel Foundry revenue rose 58%, with GAAP EPS of $0.60 and non-GAAP EPS of $0.52. Q4 guidance is $15.0–16.0 billion of revenue, with an expected PC slowdown through at least the first half of 2027. Recent deals include a multiyear Xeon collaboration with Oracle Cloud, a planned acquisition of Classiq (quantum software) and a $23 billion equity offering. CEO Lip-Bu Tan bought 150,000 shares on Nov 2 at about $64.73 (Form 4 filed Nov 4). The main risks are supply and execution: an accident at the Kiryat Gat fab in Israel will cost about $300 million of Q4 revenue, with a similar hit expected in Q1.
stocks.researchSummary: Intel's data-center demand is outrunning its supply, but a weaker PC outlook and the Israel fab accident produced soft guidance. The CEO's open-market purchase is a notable insider signal, though it is not a forecast.

flags.text: Intel lists the U.S. government's acquisition of significant equity interests in the company, along with export controls and trade policy, among its key risk factors.

Intel says demand for its data-center products 'continues to meaningfully exceed available supply', limited by Intel 3 yields, substrate shortages and the Fab 28 accident, which will cut about $300 million from Q4 revenue and 200 basis points from gross margin.

The turnaround rests on CEO Lip-Bu Tan, who has bought shares personally (150,000 on Nov 2). Client computing is still about half of Intel Products revenue ($8.1 billion of $15.4 billion), which leaves Intel exposed to the PC slowdown.

stocks.name: Amazon.com, Inc. (AWS)
stocks.overview: Amazon is the parent of AWS, the largest cloud provider, alongside its retail, Prime, advertising, devices and newer businesses (Zoox, Amazon Leo satellites, Pharmacy). In Q3 2026 AWS revenue rose 39% to $46.0 billion, its fastest growth in nearly five years and a $184 billion annualized run rate, with $17.8 billion of operating income (38.7% margin). Total net sales rose 12% to $201.9 billion, operating income was a record $28.1 billion and EPS was $1.89. AWS signed new agreements with Meta, NVIDIA, OpenAI, Oracle and others, Bedrock token volume grew nearly 17x and Trainium became easier to adopt through TorchNeuron; CEO Andy Jassy projects AWS growth above 40% in both 2027 and 2028. On Nov 5 Amazon launched $0 Uber Eats delivery for Prime members, and AWS re:Invent runs Nov 30–Dec 4 in Las Vegas. The main risk is capital intensity: 2026 cash capex of about $220 billion has pushed trailing free cash flow to an outflow of $42.4 billion.
stocks.researchSummary: AWS is accelerating on AI demand and is the main driver of Amazon's profits, while retail margins hit a record. The trade-off is very heavy AI capex funded partly with new debt, plus rising data-center permitting risk in the U.S.
stocks.cryptoLink: AWS stopped accepting new customers for Amazon Managed Blockchain (Ethereum, Bitcoin, Polygon node access) on Oct 29, 2026, and will end the service on Sep 29, 2027, pointing users to self-managed Node Runners on AWS or partners such as Alchemy and QuickNode.

Trailing-12-month free cash flow was an outflow of $42.4 billion and long-term debt rose to $173.1 billion from $65.6 billion at end-2025, as AWS competes with Google Cloud, whose revenue grew 103%, and Microsoft for AI capacity.
